solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: What might be found variously internittently in housing estates?

definitions.text: What might be found variously internittently in housing estates?

indicators.note: variously intermittently (misspelt in print) means letters are taken at irregular intervals from the words, the rest dropped

explanation.surface: A puzzle question about what grows in suburban gardens, scattered here and there.
explanation.walkthrough: Taking HO, S, TA and S at irregular intervals through 'housing estates' spells the answer; the remaining letters are dropped. 'internittently' is a misprint for 'intermittently'.
explanation.definitionFit: These leafy shade-loving garden plants are often planted in the gardens of new homes.

clue.text: Legendary footballer returning cap to accept new, bigger one from two continents?

indicators.note: returning means the footballer's name is read backwards

parts.note: Pelé was the legendary Brazilian footballer

indicators.note: to accept means the hat takes the letter for new inside it

parts.note: a cap is a kind of hat

explanation.surface: A star footballer coming back to take a new, larger international cap.
explanation.walkthrough: Pelé was Brazil's great forward; 'returning' turns his name and 'to accept' puts N in the cap. The question mark flags that the definition is playful.
explanation.definitionFit: The big land animal comes in African and Asian species, so it is found on two continents.

clue.text: Again make aware of antique car under the hammer?

indicators.note: something under the hammer is being beaten, so these letters are knocked into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An old vintage car being auctioned reminds someone of it again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'under the hammer' usually means at auction, but here it signals the letters are beaten about.
explanation.definitionFit: To renew a person's familiarity with something is to make them aware of it again.

clue.text: Suitable to cover up naked slut that's obscene in the extreme

indicators.note: to cover up means the word for suitable goes around the other piece

parts.note: best can mean most suitable

indicators.note: naked means stripped of its outer letters, leaving the middle of slut

explanation.surface: A prim remark that a filthy, unclothed woman should be covered up.
explanation.walkthrough: SLUT stripped bare leaves LU, which BEST covers. Monk said later he had read 'best' as the adjective 'suitable' by mistake.
explanation.definitionFit: Blue means smutty or indecent, so the superlative is most obscene.

clue.text: The line above a character

parts.note: the line above a person is their lineage, the forebears preceding them, not a mark printed over a letter

explanation.definitionFit: A person's forebears form the family line going back before them.

clue.text: Bird that's old, sleeping like a baby?

indicators.note: sleeping places the letter for old in the bed

parts.note: a cot is where a baby sleeps

explanation.surface: A bird that is aged and sleeps soundly, like an infant.
explanation.walkthrough: O sleeps, like a baby, in COT, a baby's bed.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a black waterbird with a white forehead shield.

clue.text: In the beginning, setter lifts spirit as discussed

indicators.note: in a down clue lifts turns the word upwards, so it is read backwards

parts.note: the setter refers to themself as me

indicators.note: as discussed means as spoken, signalling a word that sounds the same

parts.note: brio is vigour or spirit

explanation.surface: A biblical-sounding line: at the start, the compiler raises spirits as talked about.
explanation.walkthrough: ME is reversed upwards to EM; BRIO said aloud gives BRYO.
explanation.definitionFit: Something at its earliest rudimentary stage is in embryo, so it is a beginning.

clue.text: One's initially beaten by Times in old scuffle

indicators.note: in puts the letters for times inside the scuffle

parts.note: a melee is a confused scuffle or brawl
T is time, so times is two of them, TT

explanation.surface: Someone is first defeated by the clock in an old brawl.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is cryptic: eggs are beaten before this dish is cooked.
explanation.definitionFit: Eggs are whisked first to make this dish, so it starts by being beaten.

clue.text: Drilled shaft in earth, rightly using no spades

indicators.note: using no tells us to take a letter away from the word for earth

parts.note: earth or ground is soil
S is the abbreviation for spades in card games
rightly, as in properly or correctly, means well

explanation.surface: A description of a borehole sunk into the ground, dug properly without shovels.
explanation.definitionFit: A drilled shaft sunk to reach petroleum underground is the oil kind of well.

clue.text: Stir most of communal sauce

indicators.note: to stir is to mix things about, so the letters are mixed into a new order
most of says the final letter of the next word is dropped

explanation.surface: A cooking instruction: give the shared sauce a good stir, but not all of it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'most of' trims COMMUNAL to COMMUNA, and 'Stir' rearranges those seven letters.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a Vietnamese fermented fish condiment, so it is a type of sauce.

clue.text: One caught by very good subject

indicators.note: by means next to, so the two short pieces sit beside the word for very good

parts.note: top as an adjective means excellent, very good
one is the Roman numeral I
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: Someone is being taken in by an excellent theme or matter.
explanation.definitionFit: A subject of discussion is its theme or matter, a synonym.

clue.text: Regarding choices, reader in English fails regularly

indicators.note: in means the word for reader is placed inside the other letters
regularly means every other letter of the word fails is taken

parts.note: a lector is a reader, especially one reading lessons in church

explanation.surface: A remark that, when it comes to choices, a reader of English keeps failing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes the even letters of 'fails'; 'in' puts the reader inside. 'Regarding choices' reads as a link phrase but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Electoral describes votes and elections, which are matters of choosing candidates.

clue.text: Almost cut out happy Jewish feast

indicators.note: almost means the last letter of the word for cut is lost

parts.note: to shave is to cut hair close

indicators.note: happy here hints at a loose or carefree arrangement, so the letters of the next word are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone almost cut out of a joyful Jewish festival.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Almost' trims SHAVE to SHAV; 'happy' turns OUT into UOT.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the Feast of Weeks, a Jewish harvest festival held seven weeks after Passover.

clue.text: Kill surveillance when leader doesn't show up

indicators.note: the leader is the first letter, which is removed from the word for surveillance

parts.note: a stakeout is a police surveillance operation

explanation.surface: An order to murder someone, given when the boss fails to appear during a police watch.
explanation.definitionFit: To kill someone is, in gangster slang, to eliminate or rub them out.

clue.text: They'll say who can be our best, best friends

definitions.text: They'll say who can be our best, best friends

parts.words: They'll say who can be our best, best friends
parts.note: best friends are dogs, and this body judges which dog is best in show

explanation.definitionFit: The UK's governing body for dog breeding runs shows that choose the top dog.

clue.text: Now detaining a shady criminal

indicators.note: criminal suggests something crooked or bent, so the preceding letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Police are currently holding a dodgy lawbreaker.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means at the present time, in modern times, so it is a synonym of now.

clue.text: Admirer's marriage vow? Dead right

definitions.note: Admirer's reads as admirer is, the 's being a link

parts.note: I do is the vow made at a wedding
late means dead, as in the late king

explanation.surface: Asking whether a fan's wedding promise is absolutely correct.
explanation.definitionFit: A worshipper of idols, by extension an excessive admirer of someone.

clue.text: Carpenter made this chest with brilliant diamonds on top

indicators.note: on top places this letter above the rest in the down entry

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for diamonds in cards
an ark is a chest, as in the Ark of the Covenant
a star is someone brilliant

explanation.surface: A woodworker built a chest topped with sparkling gems.
explanation.walkthrough: The carpenter is John Carpenter, the film director, not a joiner.
explanation.definitionFit: This 1974 science-fiction comedy was John Carpenter's first feature film.

clue.text: Inflammation caused by removing top of sanitised cast

indicators.note: cast means thrown into a new shape, so the letters are rearranged
removing top of means the first letter of sanitised goes

explanation.surface: A medical note: soreness caused by taking off a cleaned plaster cast.
explanation.walkthrough: SANITISED loses its first S to become ANITISED, which 'cast' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: The suffix -itis means inflammation; this is the swelling of a gland.

clue.text: Fondle deciptated, gutted elver and fish

indicators.note: a misprint of decapitated: beheaded, so the first letter of the word for fondle goes

parts.note: to cosset is to pamper or fondle

indicators.note: gutted means the insides are removed, leaving only the outer letters of elver

explanation.surface: A grisly recipe: pet the beheaded, disembowelled young eel and the other fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'deciptated' is a slip for 'decapitated' in the clue as printed. COSSET loses its head; ELVER, a young eel, is gutted to ER.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a type of sturgeon, the fish prized for its caviar.

clue.text: Died in the ocean, the empty grave

indicators.note: in puts the letter for died inside the ocean

parts.note: the ocean is the sea

indicators.note: empty means hollowed out, leaving only the outer letters of the

explanation.surface: Someone died at sea, and the grave lies empty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grave' looks like a noun for burial, but it is the adjective meaning serious; 'empty' hollows out the second 'the'.
explanation.definitionFit: Grave as an adjective means serious and calm, a synonym of staid.

clue.text: Repeatedly choose dance that's genuinely not hard

parts.note: a reel is a lively Scottish dance

indicators.note: not tells us the letter for hard is left out

parts.note: echt is a German word used in English meaning genuine or authentic
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: Describing a dance that is truly easy.
explanation.walkthrough: ECHT, borrowed from German, means genuine; without H it becomes ECT.
explanation.definitionFit: To vote someone back into office means choosing them again, repeatedly.

clue.text: What news on this moralist novel following censorship of manuscript?

indicators.note: novel means new or fresh, so the remaining letters get a new arrangement
censorship cuts things out, so the letters for manuscript are removed

explanation.surface: A question about the latest from a preachy novel after a manuscript is censored.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing M and S from MORALIST leaves ORALIT, which 'novel' rearranges. Shakespeare's Shylock asks 'What news on the Rialto?' in The Merchant of Venice.
explanation.definitionFit: The Venetian bridge and market district famous from Shylock's question about the latest news.

clue.text: Sort of language to pull in The Sun's regulars

indicators.note: in places the word for pull inside the other letters
regulars means the regular letters, first, third and fifth, of The Sun

parts.note: to lug is to pull or drag

explanation.surface: A remark on the kind of words that bring in the tabloid's loyal readers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regulars' picks T, E and U from 'The Sun'; LUG goes in before the U.
explanation.definitionFit: This Dravidian tongue is spoken mainly in the Indian state of Andhra Pradesh.

clue.text: Old German, one in America, heading off somewhere in Spain

indicators.note: heading off means the first letter is removed from the word for the old German

parts.note: the Vandals were an ancient Germanic people

indicators.note: in means one letter goes inside the abbreviation for America

parts.note: USA is the United States of America
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: An old German traveller, one who has been in America, sets off for somewhere in Spain.
explanation.walkthrough: The Vandals were the Germanic tribe that sacked Rome; 'heading off' beheads them, and 'in' puts one inside the abbreviation for America.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the southernmost region of mainland Spain, home to Seville and Granada.

clue.text: Secure line and nothing else

explanation.surface: Get hold of a line and nothing more.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nothing else' joins: the letter for line plus the word 'and', with nothing more added.
explanation.definitionFit: To land a fish or a job is to secure it.

clue.text: With difficulty, children must start to relax

indicators.note: must start says this piece comes first in the answer

parts.note: CH is a dictionary abbreviation for child or children
ill, as in 'can ill afford', means with difficulty

explanation.surface: Difficult children need to begin unwinding.
explanation.definitionFit: To chill, in modern slang, is to calm down or unwind.

clue.text: Succeeded to stop excellent record about a country

indicators.note: to stop means to plug a gap, so one letter is put inside the rest
about means the pieces for excellent and record are turned round

parts.note: A1 means excellent, written here as AI
a note is a written record
S is the abbreviation for succeeded in family trees

explanation.surface: An heir succeeded in halting an outstanding record about a nation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' reverses the excellent and record pieces together, and 'to stop' plugs the succeeded letter in after the first letter. A1 for excellent is written with I as one.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a Baltic nation bordering Latvia and Russia.

clue.text: Pushily selling last place in boat trip

indicators.note: last place in means the final letter of boat is taken

parts.note: an outing is a trip or excursion

explanation.surface: Coming last in a rowing race on an excursion.
explanation.definitionFit: Touts sell tickets or wares aggressively, so the word means hawking pushily.
